Likang Life Sciences Showcases Personalized Cancer Immunotherapy and Global Ambitions at Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit 2026

Likang Life Sciences Showcases Personalized Cancer Immunotherapy and Global Ambitions at Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit 2026

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Oct. 24, 2026

BEIJING, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Likang Life Sciences ("Likang"), a biotechnology company advancing AI-enabled personalized cancer immunotherapies, sponsored and exhibited at the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit 2026, held from 20 to 22 October at ADNEC Centre Abu Dhabi. The summit marked a milestone in Likang's international outreach, showcasing its scientific platform and clinical development programs.

Convened by the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi under the theme "To Sense Is to Predict," the event brought together leaders across healthcare, research and technology.

Likang Co-Founder and Vice Chairman Shannon Cheung joined a delegation of international health leaders received by UAE President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on 20 October. He also met Abu Dhabi Crown Prince His Highness Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during his summit visit on 21 October. In brief exchanges, Cheung shared Likang's plans to bring its personalized cancer immunotherapy technologies and investigational therapies to Abu Dhabi, with a vision to develop the emirate as a platform for international research, innovation and future expansion.

Cheung spoke on "The Future of Cancer," moderated by Dr. Tarek Fadel of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), alongside Dr. Arie Belldegrun, Chairman of Bellco Health; Dr. Toni Choueiri of Harvard Medical School and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; Prof. Dr. Angela George of The Royal Marsden; and Vinicius Ribeiro, CEO of Huna.

"The future of cancer care is not just about treating cancer earlier, but treating every patient more precisely, personally and effectively," Cheung said. He discussed how genomics, AI, mRNA technology and advanced cell manufacturing could support therapies tailored to individual tumor biology, while underscoring scalability and patient access.

At Booth AD28, Likang presented its AI-enabled neoantigen discovery platform and investigational immunotherapy pipeline. Its lead candidate, LK101, a personalized neoantigen mRNA-dendritic cell therapeutic cancer vaccine, received clinical trial authorization from China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in 2023 and investigational new drug (IND) clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2025.

Building on ongoing dialogue with the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi and regional healthcare stakeholders, Likang is exploring opportunities in clinical research, AI-enabled precision oncology, scientific collaboration and potential future local manufacturing.

About Likang Life Sciences

Likang Life Sciences is a biotechnology company focused on AI-powered personalized cancer immunotherapy. Its pipeline includes personalized neoantigen therapeutic vaccines and neoantigen-specific T-cell therapies.

data.title: 'Non-answers' aren't working. This is what investors really need from the Fed.
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Chair Kevin Warsh has to make a U-turn in communication

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks during his news conference in September.

The headline coming out of the Federal Reserve's meeting Wednesday will be the central bank's decision on interest rates, but what really matters to investors, economists say, is for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to prove he can successfully communicate the central bank's strategy.

Analysts want to know whether the hot inflation readings for September were a game-changing development, and what criteria the Fed will use to assess the timing and pace of subsequent rate hikes. They'll be watching Warsh's press conference Wednesday for signs that the central bank has a strategy for curbing prices after more than five years of inflation above its 2% target.

"The market cares about the final destination," more than the outcome of Wednesday's meeting, said Juhi Dhawan, global macroanalyst at Wellington Management.

Right now, the market expects a "shallow" Fed tightening of up to three rate hikes by the end of the first quarter of 2027. There have been many periods when the Fed has tightened only a few times, she said. That strategy fits with the narrative that the Fed is reversing the three cuts the central bank made last year over concern about the labor market.

There's a possibility they could take a more aggressive approach with a full rate hike. A "full" rate-hiking cycle would be 150 or 200 basis points, Dhawan said, which would take rates back up to the highest levels since 2023.

Derek Tang, co-founder of forecasting firm LH Meyer, said the market has a very difficult time understanding when the rate hikes will end.

"Do the hikes end when inflation literally is at 2%?" Tang asked.

Previous Fed chairs have provided a forecast, such as saying something like: The Fed can hike until underlying inflation gets low enough and then the central bank will hold rates steady. But Warsh hasn't provided any signals about the Fed's approach.

"It is a little bit of a black box," Tang said. "He's become quite skilled at giving non-answers."

The ultimate level of rates will impact borrowers and homebuyers. If rates go high enough, it could even choke off the current economic expansion.

A less-is-more approach

When Warsh came into office in May, he installed a sea change in Fed communication that can best be summed up as "less is more." A quieter Fed would let the market speak louder, he said.

This approach has proven to be a mistake, said Nicholas Economides, a professor of economics at the Stern School of Business at New York University.

"The new Fed chair has missed his chance to define policy coherently by proposing to 'listen to the market,' when the market in fact wants to listen to him," Economides said in an interview.

Warsh's silence on his views on the path forward for interest rates essentially gives away the Fed's authority to the market, he added.

"Unless the Fed speaks authoritatively, over and above what market considerations are, it will just lose its voice," Economides said.

He pointed to market moves after the Fed's September rate hike as an example.

At his September press conference, Warsh declined to answer whether he thought the first hike in three years would be a one-off event or the start of a series of hikes.

Without any guidance, markets pushed interest rates on longer-term Treasurys significantly higher, with the 10-year yield rising to 5.3%, as the market priced in an aggressive Fed with a rate hike in October.

-Greg Robb

data.title: NANOBIOTIX Announces Final Data from Phase 1 Study Evaluating JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors as a 2L+ Therapy in Anti-PD-1-Resistant Primary Cutaneous Melanoma
data.description:
• In 24 heavily pre-treated patients with advanced primary cutaneous melanoma whose cancer had progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy including anti-PD-1 therapy, data continue to show an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy
  • 41.7% (10/24) overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1, including 4 complete responses
  • 75% (18/24) disease control rate (DCR)
  • 17.8 months median Overall Survival
  • Exploratory analysis in a subset of patients (n=8) identified IL-1β, a cytokine linked to treatment-induced anti-tumor immunity, as the most increased plasma cytokine after treatment
  • Investigators concluded that these preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in randomized clinical trials for patients with primary cutaneous melanoma naïve or refractory to anti-PD-1

Data presented at the 2026 Congress of the European Society for Medical Oncology

PARIS and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NANOBIOTIX (Euronext: NANO - NASDAQ: NBTX - the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biotechnology company pioneering physics-based approaches to expand treatment possibilities for patients with cancer and other major diseases, today announced updated results from patients with anti-PD-1-resistant advanced primary cutaneous melanoma treated in the ongoing Phase 1 Study 1100. The study evaluates JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3), which works in the presence of radiotherapy, followed by an immune checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) in patients with advanced solid tumors. The data were presented by Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center, in a poster session on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (“ESMO”) in Madrid, Spain.

ABSTRACT #3956: Safety and Anti-Tumor Activity of NBTXR3/SBRT with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Anti-PD-1 Resistant Melanoma: Results from a Phase I Dose Expansion

J. Chan, J. Lee, A. Lam, A. Daud, F. Collichio, H. Yu, P. Mody, J. Weiss, S. Moschos, S. Powell, S. Peck, M. Lohr, E. Redstone, Z. Li, W. Smith, A. Juloori, R. Gineste, D. Rolando, A. Rosenberg and C. Shen. UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center; UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Sanford Cancer Center; St Luke's University Hospital; The University of Chicago; Nanobiotix

Patients with advanced anti-PD-1 resistant primary cutaneous melanoma whose disease has progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy have a poor prognosis; published series report a median progression-free survival of approximately three months1 and a median overall survival of approximately one year2 in this setting. Melanoma has historically been considered radioresistant, and higher radiation doses are often limited by exposure of the surrounding healthy tissue.

“Patients whose melanoma has progressed on anti-PD-1 therapy, and often on several other immunotherapies as well, have limited options left,” said Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center “In this study, a single injection followed by a short course of stereotactic radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of tumor sizes and locations, and we saw responses in lesions that were injected and in lesions that were not. The observed increase in IL-1β suggests treatment-related immune activation that warrants further investigation. These are early data from a single-arm study, and they support testing the approach in a randomized trial.”

All 24 heavily pre-treated patients had advanced primary cutaneous melanoma resistant to anti-PD-1; 14 had stage IV disease. Most had received other immunotherapies before enrolling, including anti-CTLA-4 (50%), anti-LAG-3 (33.3%) and T-VEC (25%), and 87.5% had received immunotherapy as their most recent therapy. Patients received a one-time intratumoral injection of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) at the recommended Phase 2 dose (33% of gross tumor volume), followed by stereotactic body radiotherapy (“SBRT”) to the injected lesion and then nivolumab or pembrolizumab. Investigators observed an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy.

Safety and Feasibility

Treatment consisting of a single intratumoral JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) injection, followed by a short course of radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of melanoma lesions, providing a minimally invasive treatment approach with an acceptable safety profile. No new safety signals have been observed.

Preliminary Efficacy

An Overall Response Rate (ORR) of 41.7% (10/24 patients) was observed. Responses were observed in both injected (ORR 45.8%; 11/24 evaluable patients) and non-injected lesions (ORR 30.0%; 3/10 evaluable patients).

Median Progression Free Survival (PFS) was 6.9 months, while median Overall Survival reached 17.8 months.

Exploratory Immune Profiling

In an exploratory analysis of plasma samples from a subset of patients (n=8), IL-1β showed the largest increase from baseline among the cytokines evaluated. Published research has linked IL-1β to treatment-induced anti-tumor immunity through its role in connecting innate immune activation to the priming of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells.3

"This updated analysis, with more patients and longer follow-up, builds on the first data we reported with consistent safety and an improvement in Overall Survival relative to the first data reported," said Louis Kayitalire, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Nanobiotix. "Responses were again seen in patients whose disease had progressed after multiple prior therapies, including in lesions that were not injected. Together with the exploratory cytokine data, these findings warrant further evaluation of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) followed by anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma."

Overall, the acceptable safety profile and early efficacy observed by investigators in these preliminary findings provide promising signals of activity and warrant further evaluation in larger randomized trials.

About JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)

JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) is a novel, potentially first-in-class oncology product composed of functionalized hafnium oxide nanoparticles administered via one-time intratumoral injection and designed to work in the presenced of radiotherapy. The product candidate’s mechanism of action (MoA) is designed to induce significant tumor cell death in the injected tumor when in the presence of radiotherapy, subsequently triggering adaptive immune response and long-term anti-cancer memory. Proof-of-concept was demonstrated in a randomized Phase 2/3 soft tissue sarcoma study sponsored by Nanobiotix in 2018.

JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) is being evaluated across multiple solid tumor indications as a single agent or combination therapy. Given the Company’s focus areas, and balanced against the scalable potential of NBTXR3, Nanobiotix has engaged in a collaboration strategy to expand development of the product candidate in parallel with its priority development pathways. Pursuant to this strategy, in 2019 Nanobiotix entered into a broad, comprehensive clinical research collaboration with The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center to sponsor several Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies evaluating JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) across tumor types and therapeutic combinations.

In February 2020, the United States Food and Drug Administration granted regulatory Fast Track designation for the investigation of NBTXR3 with or without cetuximab, for the treatment of patients with locally advanced HNSCC who are not eligible for platinum-based chemotherapy.

In 2023, Nanobiotix announced a license agreement for the global development and commercialization of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) with Janssen Pharmaceutica NV, a Johnson & Johnson company. Studies being led by Johnson & Johnson include NANORAY-312 (NCT04892173), a global, randomized Phase 3 study in platinum-based chemotherapy-ineligible, locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancers; LUMIRAY (NCT07219212), a global, phase 1b, open-label study in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancers; and CONVERGE (NCT06667908), a phase 2, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study in locally advanced and unresectable Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

About NANOBIOTIX

Nanobiotix is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company pioneering disruptive, physics-based therapeutic approaches to revolutionize treatment outcomes for millions of patients; supported by people committed to making a difference for humanity. The Company’s philosophy is rooted in the concept of pushing past the boundaries of what is known to expand possibilities for human life.

Incorporated in 2003, Nanobiotix is headquartered in Paris, France and is listed on Euronext Paris since 2012 and on the Nasdaq Global Select Market in New York City since December 2020. The Company has subsidiaries in Cambridge, Massachusetts (United States) amongst other locations.

data.title: Genmab and Incyte Announce Clinical Trial Collaboration in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
data.description:
Genmab and Incyte Announce Clinical Trial Collaboration in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

  • Phase 1/2 study will evaluate petosemtamab plus INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in first-line KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC)

Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and Incyte (Nasdaq: INCY) today announced a clinical trial collaboration to evaluate petosemtamab, Genmab’s investigational IgG1-bispecific antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5), in combination with INCB161734, Incyte’s investigational, potent and selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, and standard-of-care chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring a KRAS G12D mutation, an area with substantial unmet medical need.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261024542855/en/

“This collaboration supports our broader development strategy for petosemtamab as we explore its potential across treatment settings and in novel combinations,” said Judith Klimovsky, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Development Officer, Genmab. “Partnering with Incyte enables us to evaluate this investigational combination in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer, reflecting our commitment to research collaborations aimed at expanding potential treatment options for more patients.”

“Metastatic colorectal cancer remains difficult-to-treat, underscoring the importance of evaluating novel combinations grounded in complementary scientific approaches with the potential to enhance efficacy,” said Pablo J. Cagnoni, M.D., President, Incyte and Global Head of Research and Development. “Our collaboration with Genmab will explore the potential of combining KRAS G12D inhibition with LGR5-targeted EGFR inhibition and standard-of-care chemotherapy, with the goal of advancing a new first-line treatment approach for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer.”

Under the collaboration, Genmab will conduct the Phase 1/2 study evaluating petosemtamab in combination with INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated mCRC in the first-line setting. Incyte will co-fund the study and provide clinical supply of INCB161734.

KRAS mutations occur in approximately 40% of colorectal cancers, with G12D being the most common KRAS mutation. These cancers are associated with poor prognosis, underscoring the need for new treatment approaches. The collaboration reflects a shared focus on investigating whether agents with distinct and potentially complementary mechanisms, combined with standard-of-care chemotherapy, may offer a path toward a new treatment option for patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer.

About Petosemtamab (GEN1158)
Petosemtamab is an investigational human IgG1-based bispecific antibody targeting the EGFR and the LGR5 and designed to support multiple anti-tumor mechanisms. It inhibits EGFR-mediated signaling by engaging a unique site on the receptor to prevent ligand binding. In addition, petosemtamab triggers EGFR degradation in cancer stem-like cells expressing both EGFR and LGR5. Petosemtamab is also engineered to enhance innate immune-mediated activity through interactions with macrophages and natural killer cells. It is currently being investigated in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and other solid tumors, including colorectal cancer (CRC). Petosemtamab is being evaluated in combination with chemotherapy in two Phase 3 trials in first- and second-line RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic CRC. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

About INCB161734
INCB161734 is an investigational, novel, selective and orally bioavailable small molecule ON/OFF KRAS G12D inhibitor. KRAS is one of the most frequently altered oncogenic drivers across solid tumors, and the KRAS G12D mutation is among the most common KRAS alterations, occurring in approximately 40% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and approximately 15% of colorectal cancer (CRC) cases.

INCB161734 is being evaluated in the global Phase 3 DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) study which is currently enrolling patients with previously untreated KRAS G12D-mutated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of INCB161734 in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy.

INCB161734 is also being evaluated as a monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy (gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel [GEMNabP] or modified FOLFIRINOX [mFOLFIRINOX]), in an ongoing open-label Phase 1 study across KRAS G12D-mutated solid tumors (NCT06179160).

About Genmab
Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com or follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Incyte is redefining what’s possible in biopharmaceutical innovation. Through deep scientific expertise and a relentless focus on patients, we have built an established portfolio of first-in-class medicines and an extensive portfolio of next-generation medicines across our key franchises: Hematology, Oncology and Inflammation & Autoimmunity.

Best AI Tools for Marketing Content (2026): CapCut Recognized for Faster AI-Powered Video and Image Creation by Better Business Advice

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Oct. 24, 2026

NEW YORK, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Better Business Advice has recognized CapCut in its 2026 coverage of the best AI tools for marketing content, highlighting its collection of AI-powered features for creating and editing videos, images, audio, and other campaign assets. The recognition reflects growing interest in tools that help transform creative concepts into usable marketing materials while reducing the manual work involved in production.

Best AI Marketing Tools

  • Seedance 2.0 - an AI video generation model that creates videos from text prompts or images
  • Seedream - an AI image generation model that creates high-quality visuals from text prompts

AI-powered content creation is changing how businesses develop digital marketing campaigns. From promotional videos and product imagery to social media graphics and branded audio, organizations face growing demand for creative assets across multiple digital channels. Tools that simplify production and support faster experimentation are becoming an increasingly important part of modern marketing workflows.

CapCut offers a range of AI-assisted capabilities covering several stages of content creation. These include text-based video generation, AI image generation, background removal, image expansion, music generation, and photo animation. Together, the tools provide options for producing marketing assets for social media, digital advertising, product promotions, and other online campaigns.

AI Video Generation Supports Promotional Campaigns

Video is an important format for communicating product information, presenting services, and building audience engagement. However, producing video content regularly can require significant planning, editing, and creative resources.

CapCut's Seedance 2.0 AI video generator supports prompt-based video creation. Users can describe a creative concept and generate video content that serves as a starting point for further development.

The capability can support promotional videos, product showcases, educational content, and social media campaigns. It also gives creators a way to explore different visual approaches during the planning stage before refining the selected direction.

For businesses producing content across multiple channels, AI-assisted video generation can help reduce the effort required to develop initial concepts. Generated material can then be reviewed and edited to align with campaign objectives, brand guidelines, and platform requirements.

Image Generation Helps Develop Marketing Concepts

Visual assets influence how products, services, and campaigns are presented to audiences. Developing suitable imagery often involves several rounds of brainstorming and creative testing before a final direction is selected.

CapCut's Seedream AI image generator enables users to create images from text prompts. The tool can support concept drafts, campaign planning, and experimentation with different visual styles.

For example, a seasonal marketing campaign may require several approaches to backgrounds, compositions, and visual themes. AI-generated drafts can help illustrate those options before resources are committed to final production.

CapCut's GPT Image 2 provides another option for generating images from natural language instructions. The feature can support the development of promotional graphics, campaign imagery, and other visual assets.

These tools help shorten the early stages of creative development by making it easier to turn written ideas into visual references. Human review remains important to ensure the resulting assets accurately represent the product and meet the campaign's requirements.

Image Editing Simplifies Asset Preparation

AI image generation is only one part of preparing content for publication. Existing photographs and graphics often need adjustments before they can be used across marketing channels.

CapCut's AI background removal tool helps separate subjects from their original backgrounds. This can be useful when preparing product images, promotional graphics, and other assets that require a different visual setting.

The AI Image Extender addresses the challenge of adapting images to different layouts. By generating content beyond an image's original boundaries, the tool can help users adjust compositions for different formats without relying entirely on cropping or stretching.

“The additional data from Study 2 of VIKTORIA-1 show consistent and significant clinical benefit for important sub-groups of breast cancer patients treated with gedatolisib regimens,” said Igor Gorbachevsky, Chief Medical Officer of Celcuity. “For patients who do not have liver metastases and received the gedatolisib triplet, the median progression-free survival was approximately 21 months, versus approximately 9 months for the alpelisib regimen. VIKTORIA-1 PIK3CA Wild-Type Cohort Comparative Analysis

Dr. Sara Tolaney, Chief of the Division of Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, presented a comparative analysis of data for the gedatolisib regimens from the PIK3CA wild-type cohort of VIKTORIA-1 and other regimens evaluated in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.

Poster 1873P: Gedatolisib (Ged) vs Other Regimens Post-CDK4/6i and Endocrine Therapy (ET) in PIK3CA Wild-Type (WT) HR+/ HER2- Advanced Breast Cancer (aBC): A Network Meta-Analysis (NMA)

Eight studies were included in this network meta-analysis comparing progression-free survival outcomes in randomized controlled trials of systemic treatments evaluated among patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer with CDK4/6 inhibitor experience and PIK3CA wild-type tumors. This analysis found that the gedatolisib triplet and doublet each demonstrated statistically significant or numerically superior improvement in PFS and in progression-free survival rate at 6 months relative to the non-gedatolisib regimens evaluated. Of note, the analysis found that patients treated with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet were a statistically significant 2x and 1.5x more likely to survive without disease progression or death compared to imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, respectively.

About HR+/HER2- Breast Cancer

Breast cancer is the second most common cancer and one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1 More than two million breast cancer cases were diagnosed globally in 2022.1 While survival rates are high for those diagnosed with early breast cancer, only approximately 30% of patients who are diagnosed with or who progress to metastatic disease are expected to live five years after their diagnosis.2 HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most common subtype of breast cancer, accounting for approximately 70% of all breast cancers.2

Celcuity is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications. The company's first FDA-approved product is REVTORPYK™ (gedatolisib), pan-PI3K and mTORC1/2 inhibitor that comprehensively blockades the PAM (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway. Its mechanism of action and pharmacokinetic properties are differentiated from other currently approved and investigational therapies that target PI3Kα, AKT or mTORC1 alone or together. A Phase 3 clinical trial, VIKTORIA-1, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with fulvestrant with or without palbociclib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, supported FDA approval of REVTORPYK for use in patients without a PIK3CA mutation detected following progression on or after treatment with at least one line of endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting. Results for the PIK3CA mutant cohort of VIKTORIA-1 have been released. VIKTORIA-2 is an ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial incorporating two independent studies, Study 1 and Study 2, in two separate cohorts of patients with ABC who are treatment-naive in the advanced setting. Study 1 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- ABC. Study 2 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus letrozole as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-sensitive HR+/HER2- ABC. data.title: Compass Therapeutics Announces Publication of Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 Results for Tovecimig in the Journal of Clinical Oncology and Oral Presentation at ESMO 2026
data.description:
• As published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO) and presented at ESMO, COMPANION-002 met its primary endpoint of ORR and key secondary endpoint of PFS, with a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.
  • Responses were durable, with a median duration of response (DOR) of 4.9 months, and disease control rate (DCR) was also significantly improved (62.2% vs. 36.8%).
  • A new, post hoc analysis of overall survival (OS) included in the JCO publication uses the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, and demonstrates an OS hazard ratio of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Safety profile was consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified.

BOSTON, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CMPX), a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases, today announced the publication of results from the positive Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study of tovecimig in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO). The results are also being presented today by Nilofer S. Azad, M.D., Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid, Spain. The full publication is available via open access at https://ascopubs.org/toc/jco/0/ja.

COMPANION-002 is a randomized Phase 2/3 study that evaluated tovecimig plus paclitaxel versus paclitaxel alone in 168 patients with advanced BTC who had received one prior therapy. As previously reported, and now published following peer review, the study met its primary endpoint, with tovecimig plus paclitaxel demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in ORR of 18.0% vs. 5.3% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0228) evaluated by blinded independent central review (BICR). The study also met its key secondary endpoint of PFS with a median PFS of 4.7 vs. 2.6 months (HR=0.44, p<0.0001), representing a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.

Key findings from COMPANION-002 include:

  • Duration of response and disease control: Responses with tovecimig plus paclitaxel lasted a median of 4.9 months. The disease control rate, which includes patients whose cancer responded or remained stable, significantly improved at 62.2% vs. 36.8% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0018).
  • Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma subgroup: Patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (cancer of the bile ducts inside the liver), a prespecified subgroup, made up more than half of the study population (92 of 168). In these patients, results were consistent with the overall study population, with an ORR of 15.3% vs. 0% (p=0.0258) and median PFS of 5.1 vs. 3.0 months (HR=0.32).
  • Overall survival (OS) and crossover-adjusted analysis: Patients in the paclitaxel arm could cross over to tovecimig plus paclitaxel arm after BICR-confirmed progression. 31 of 57 (54%) patients crossed over, resulting in 85% of all patients in the study (142 of 168) ultimately receiving tovecimig. The intent-to-treat OS analysis was confounded by the high rate of crossover and no statistically significant difference in OS was observed. To estimate the treatment effect if crossover had not occurred, the JCO publication includes a post hoc exploratory analysis using the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, in which the OS hazard ratio was 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Outcomes in crossover patients: Among the 31 patients who crossed over, median PFS after the addition of tovecimig to paclitaxel, a prespecified secondary endpoint, was 3.5 months, compared with 1.9 months during their initial treatment with paclitaxel alone (HR=0.40, p=0.0035). In a post hoc exploratory analysis, these patients who crossed over to receive tovecimig had a median OS of 12.8 months, compared with 6.1 months for control-arm patients who did not cross over (HR=0.54, p=0.04), even though crossover patients had progressed more quickly on initial paclitaxel treatment. These crossover comparisons were not randomized and are exploratory.
  • Safety: The safety profile was generally manageable and consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in the combination arm were hypertension (69%) and fatigue (67%). Grade 3 or higher TEAEs occurred in 93.5% of patients in the combination arm and 64.2% of patients who received paclitaxel alone. TEAEs leading to overall treatment discontinuation occurred in 27.8% and 11.3%, respectively, and were mostly consistent with known anti-angiogenic and chemotherapy toxicities. No hypertensive crises or unexpected severe cardiovascular toxicities were observed. TEAEs leading to death occurred in 5.6% and 1.9% of patients, respectively.

“COMPANION-002 is an important, randomized study in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer,” said Dr. Azad. “The significant improvements in response rate and progression-free survival, together with the durability of responses and disease control, are encouraging for patients in this setting. We also saw activity in patients who switched to tovecimig after their disease progressed on paclitaxel alone, which is notable in a setting where disease often progresses quickly.”

"Publication of the COMPANION-002 results in the Journal of Clinical Oncology following independent peer review is a significant milestone for patients with BTC," said Thomas Schuetz, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Compass. "These data, including the new two-stage estimation adjusting for the crossover impact on overall survival, strengthen our conviction that tovecimig has the potential to make a meaningful difference for patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer who have few treatment options. We are determined to bring tovecimig to these patients and will continue working with the FDA toward that goal."

Additional analyses from COMPANION-002, including patient-reported quality of life and translational research, are ongoing and will be reported separately.

About Tovecimig
Tovecimig is an investigational DLL4 x VEGF-A bispecific antibody designed to block two angiogenic pathways simultaneously, representing a first-in-class approach to disrupting tumor angiogenesis. In COMPANION-002, tovecimig was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer. Tovecimig has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Tovecimig remains investigational and has not been approved by the FDA.

About Biliary Tract Cancer
BTC is an aggressive, life-threatening cancer estimated to affect approximately 26,500 patients annually in the United States. For the vast majority of patients with BTC whose tumors do not harbor an actionable mutation with an approved targeted therapy, there is currently no FDA-approved treatment in the second-line setting. The therapies most commonly used in this setting, which are not labeled or approved by the FDA for the treatment of patients with BTC, generally have an ORR of approximately 5% or less.

About COMPANION-002
COMPANION-002 (NCT05506943) is a randomized, controlled Phase 2/3 study of tovecimig in patients with unresectable advanced, metastatic or recurrent BTC who received one prior systemic chemotherapy regimen. The study randomized 168 patients 2:1 to tovecimig plus paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). The primary endpoint was ORR by blinded independent central review; secondary endpoints included PFS, OS and duration of response.

data.title: 'She's living the dream': My stepmother said I can buy my childhood home for $850,000. Is she taking advantage of me?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s'

"She said if my dad wanted me to have it, he should have arranged that before he died." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s. By the time he died, it was worth about $850,000, mostly because it's spacious and in a good neighborhood. He left it to my stepmother, whom he married a few years after my mom died. She is now 74. They were together for 18 years. She took care of him through the whole illness, which I don't take lightly.

Dad told me more than once that the house would be mine someday. My stepmother now wants to sell and move somewhere smaller. She's living the dream in Miami. I offered $700,000. That's $200,000 under market, but I thought it was fair, given that she would skip agent fees and it would be a quick, clean sale. I'd have to stretch to do it, but I could manage.

She was really offended, and she told me as much. She said she's paid the property taxes and the repairs for years (she put a new roof on in 2021). She also said she spent a big chunk of her own savings on my father's care and that the house is basically her retirement plan, and that she can't just hand me $200,000 because I'm sentimental.

Don't miss: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

The $200,000 discount

That's a fair point, and I told her so. What I can't get past is that a few years ago she gave her daughter $200,000 toward a house, and that is how (and why) I came up with the $200,000 haircut on my father's home. I brought that up, and she said things were different then, and pointed out that I have a good job and can buy my own place.

She said if my dad wanted me to have it, he should have arranged that before he died. As my girlfriend at the time said, "Yes, she really went there." That comment really stung. He trusted her with everything, and it feels like his wishes just evaporated. She says she honored him by caring for him and that I'm discounting everything she sacrificed.

I could, of course, walk away and buy somewhere else. I've even looked at a couple of listings. But it wouldn't be the same, and I'd always feel like the house slipped away from our family. I know that my stepsister's place has a sauna in the basement, and I'd bet anything that my stepmother helped pay for that too. Not that I'm keeping score. (OK, I know I am a little.)

Am I being unreasonable?

The Stepson

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My wife never went back to work after raising our kids. Do I have to share my retirement savings 50/50?

You can't force someone to sell you a house that never legally belonged to you.

Dear Stepson,

Don't allow steam from your stepsister's sauna to cloud your vision. You can grieve the loss of your childhood home without assigning blame.

What's more, you can't force someone to sell you a house that never belonged to you in the first place. Your childhood home, legally and morally, belonged to your father. Even though you grew up there, that doesn't give you the right to a life estate or a $200,000 discount on the purchase price because your stepmother gave her daughter $200,000 toward the down payment on her own home. What's more, selling a house to a family member below fair market value can create a gift of equity equal to the price difference, which the IRS may treat as a taxable gift.

Your late father made a promise that he did not keep, could not keep or decided not to keep. That was his responsibility. It's not your stepmother's job to make good on your father's promises. Whether he made a will leaving her the house or whether she inherited the house through state intestate laws, the end result is the same: She legally owns the house, and she has the right to live there or sell it to whomever she wants.

It is your belief that your father's wishes "evaporated." But wishes, promises and/or intentions evolve, and perhaps he realized that he wanted to take care of his wife of nearly two decades, and die with the knowledge that she would always have a roof over her head. It would have been better to have discussed those plans with you rather than leaving you in a kind of limbo, wondering if he truly wanted to leave his estate to his wife. Chances are, he did.

That does not mean this is an easy or pleasant situation for you. You have an emotional attachment to this property, and you regard your stepmother as an interloper, inheriting a property where your own mother probably once lived. It's a tough break for you and your siblings, if you have any. You made your stepmother an offer and she declined. She may be thinking about her own retirement and financial future.

Don't miss: 'I don't feel sorry for myself': I'm 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?

Passing judgment

Two decades is a long time to spend with someone. She met your father when she was in her 50s, and she's now rightly concerned about medical costs, if she needs nursing home care, especially if she does not have long-term care insurance, or any other kind of life insurance. This house may be the only asset she has, and downsizing will give her a cushion as she heads towards her 80th birthday in six years. That's quite a reality check.

I'm heartened that you realize that taking care of your father was no small deal for your stepmother. Who will take care of her if she sells you this house for $650,000 and runs out of money? Will you drive her to hospital appointments and spend hours a day with her, making sure that she takes her medication and pays her bills, and has enough to eat? That might sound dramatic, but getting older often comes with health complications.

One could argue that you both "went there." She "went there" by telling you your father wanted her to have his house. You "went there" by using emotional leverage, whether or not you believe it in your heart to be valid, to persuade her to sell this house to you on the cheap. By doing so, you are, whether you realize it or not, also passing judgment on her marriage of 18 years to a man she probably loved very much. You both spoke plainly. That's OK. Just know it's 50/50.

If you want this house, put in an offer when it is listed for sale. If she does get more than one offer and, say, one party offers $50,000 more, she may still decide to sell you the house (and maybe not even mention that she is selling it to you at less than the other offer). Remember, if she gets $950,000 rather than $850,000 - a real possibility if it's a cash buyer and it's a sought-after neighborhood - she would have been giving you a $300,000 discount if she agreed to your proposal.

All is fair in love, second marriages, legal beneficiaries and real estate. Just don't overstretch yourself financially for the sake of nostalgia.

data.title: My spouse was awarded $90,000 from my 401(k) in our divorce. How is that fair?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I retired in 2020 and subsequently went through a divorce a few years later'

"Earlier in my career, while I was still working, I went through another divorce. I was able to replenish the funds distributed from my retirement plan on a pretax basis." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I retired in 2020 and subsequently went through a divorce a few years later. As part of the division of assets, approximately $90,000 was awarded to my ex-spouse from my 401(k). Is this normal, and does that kind of arrangement sound fair to you?

Earlier in my career, while I was still working, I went through another divorce. I was able to replenish the funds distributed from my retirement plan on a pretax basis, in addition to making my regular contributions. Is it possible to do something similar now that I am retired?

Happily and Unhappily Divorced

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

Life will be easier for you if you make peace with the outcome.

Dear Divorced,

You hit on something that comes up a lot in divorce: fairness versus acceptance.

The former is adjudicated by the judge in the proceedings. They make their ruling using the letter of the law - evaluating marital property and what the lower-earning spouse contributed to the marriage. In recent weeks, I have received letters from readers who have balked over splitting their retirement funds with an estranged spouse who gave up their career to stay at home, raise their children and run their household - often a job that has no official start or end time. I'm curious to know what percentage of your 401(k) that $90,000 made up.

Ultimately, I leave you to decide whether this $90,000 distribution was fair because you're the one who has to live with the court's decision. Life will be easier for you if you make peace with the outcome; otherwise, every time you decide not to upgrade your flight, not take a vacation or not spend money on a shiny object, you run the risk of harking back to this moment in divorce court when your 401(k) was suddenly $90,000 lighter. Divorce is not just about legal and financial separation; the most challenging part of all is emotional separation and closure.

As Tracy Callahan - co-founder of the Divorce Coaches Academy, an organization that helps people journey through the most painful and challenging parts of the process - points out in this podcast, the hardest part of a divorce agreement is having to live with it. "I think about settlement agreements the same way I think about buying shoes," she says. "When you buy a pair of shoes, you don't buy them because they look good sitting on the shelf. You buy them because you're going to have to walk in them. The same is true with divorce agreements."

Understanding the legal basis for the $90,000 award to your ex-spouse may help. Contributions made to your 401(k) and IRA during a marriage, including returns on the principal, are often considered marital property, unless otherwise stated in a prenuptial agreement. Funds contributed before the marriage, after your legal separation or received as an inheritance are usually regarded as separate property. Equitable-distribution states divide assets equitably, but not necessarily 50/50, while community-property states aim to divide marital property 50/50.

Don't miss: We have a $300,000 mortgage with a 2.75% interest rate. I want to pay it off. My husband says I'm crazy. Who's right?

Limits and rules for 401(k)s

These instructions from the Internal Revenue Service sum it up: "If a plan participant gets divorced, his or her ex-spouse may become entitled to a portion of the participant's retirement-account balance. Depending on the type of plan and the amount of benefits, the ex-spouse may have immediate access to his or her portion of those assets or at some point in the future (usually upon the participant's retirement or death). Most plans require an ex-spouse to file a Qualified Domestic Relations Order with the plan administrator before the plan can pay."

After your divorce, it sounds like you boosted your 401(k) contributions based on the terms of your employer-sponsored plan. But limits apply: In 2026, workers can contribute up to $24,500 a year to a 401(k) from their own paycheck, with pretax and Roth contributions counting toward that limit. If you're 50 or older, you can make an additional $8,000 annual catch-up contribution ($32,500 in total), and workers ages 60 to 63 can get an annual $11,250 catch-up ($35,750 in total). Employee and employer contributions can reach $72,000, excluding any catch-ups.

You can usually only contribute to a 401(k) while you are still working. You can, however, rollover your money from your 401(k) to an IRA. People do this to simplify their retirement portfolio, so all their investments are in one place, and also to access a broader range of investments in an IRA. When you roll over money from your 401(k) into an IRA, you won't pay taxes on the rollover itself, but you will pay income taxes when you eventually draw down money from your IRA in retirement - so your investments continue to grow tax-deferred in the meantime.

Vanguard highlights some things to consider before a rollover. "While IRAs can have low fees, your employer-plan fees may be even lower," it says. "You should review your plan's fee structure and the IRA fee structure to determine which might be the most cost-effective. Some 401(k) plans offer institutional shares, which could have lower expense ratios than those of funds typically held in an IRA. If you leave your employer between ages 55 and 591/2, you may take penalty-free withdrawals from your 401(k). IRAs require that you wait until age 591/2."

I wish you a prosperous and resentment-free retirement as you navigate life as a single man.
